outcome: confirmed PostgreSQL production selection bug; corrected in scope; E5 fixture expectations also need correction

root_cause.mechanism: Native and accepted reported cost observations use point coverage represented as start plus 1ns. PostgreSQL TIMESTAMP precision collapses both values to the same microsecond. usageSegmentNativeOverlapTx required coverage_end > nativeStart, so PostgreSQL rejected the exact matching point as non-overlapping. The accepted external CostBundle was selected earlier, then discarded during native group-state construction. Canonical facts kept the native token source but had unknown cost, and the public aggregate cost stayed null.

confirmed_postgresql_observations.before_fix: The exact work identity and point-coverage case returned null aggregate cost on PostgreSQL. The accepted plugin cost candidate and matching selection group were present, but the native overlap lookup returned false after timestamp precision collapsed the interval. The published fact retained native token provenance with cost unknown.
confirmed_postgresql_observations.after_fix: The same admitted native-plus-reported-cost workflow returns 150 tokens and 1200 subcents for matching identity and point coverage. Native token source/actor and plugin cost source remain separately represented in canonical facts.
confirmed_postgresql_observations.unrelated_report: A separately accepted 1200-subcent cost with unrelated work identity leaves the native event's applicable unknown cost intact, so the public aggregate cost remains null.

root_cause.change: The overlap predicate now accepts exact equality for coverage keys explicitly marked point:<...>, while retaining the existing interval overlap logic. CostMetricAbsent semantics were not inverted.

fixture_findings.observation: 150 known tokens with no selected price produce CostMetricAbsent=false and nil CostSubcents: cost is unknown but applicable.
fixture_findings.correction: Change the pre-price assertion to expect applicable unknown cost. Do not expect CostMetricAbsent=true.

fixture_findings.case: auth cost report and public aggregate
fixture_findings.observation: The accepted 1200-subcent price uses a fresh provider_event identity and timestamp, unrelated to the already retained native token event. The public all-time aggregate correctly remains null because that native event still has unknown applicable cost.
fixture_findings.correction: For an aggregate-positive-price assertion, report against the native event's exact provider_event identity and occurrence time. If the price is intentionally unrelated, expect aggregate cost to remain unknown. A direct canonical fact/source assertion can verify a standalone cost-only observation.

fixture_findings.observation: The desktop sharedCost report already uses the native event identity and same ObservedAt, which satisfies the matching work/coverage contract once the pre-price expectation is corrected and the PostgreSQL overlap fix is deployed.
